monthly_review.summary: This month shows a clear shift toward lower-intensity, higher-volume aerobic base work — evidenced by increased Z1/Z2 time and reduced HR — but at the cost of pace consistency and recent speed exposure.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone distribution shifted dramatically: Z1+Z2 rose from 55% to 82% while Z4+Z5 collapsed from 19% to 2%, indicating near-total absence of threshold or VO2 max stimulus this month.

goal_tracker.message: You need 9.3 more km across 3 remaining sessions (avg 3.1 km/session) to match last month’s 38.0 km — achievable with one longer run (e.g., 5.5 km) and two moderate runs (e.g., 2.0–2.5 km each).

insights.title: Efficiency declined despite lower HR
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency dropped from 13.66 m/beat (Apr) to 13.43 m/beat (May), even though avg HR fell 7 bpm — suggesting less effective oxygen utilization per heartbeat, possibly due to reduced neuromuscular coordination or pacing inconsistency.

insights.title: Near-zero high-intensity stimulus
insights.body: Z4 and Z5 combined dropped from 19% of time last month (15% Z4 + 4% Z5) to just 2% this month (2% Z4, 0% Z5), meaning no VO2 max or race-pace efforts occurred in May — a critical gap for maintaining speed endurance.

insights.title: Cadence improved but stride length and vertical oscillation diverged
insights.body: Cadence rose from 142 to 144 spm, yet stride length increased sharply on 2026-05-16 (94.35 m) — paired with lowest ground contact (286 ms) and highest vertical oscillation (8.1 cm) — indicating an inefficient, bouncy effort likely driven by fatigue or poor pacing control.

insights.title: Reduced load coincides with slower recent pace
insights.body: The 2026-05-16 run (7:45 min/km, 148 bpm) was the fastest pace this month but occurred after only 2.5 km and showed elevated VO2 max (37.0) — yet it followed three consecutive days of sub-10 min/km running, suggesting accumulated fatigue may be compromising sustainable pace development.

recommendations.action: Do a 4.5 km Zone 2 run (HR 128–138 bpm) on your next run, holding cadence steady at 145–147 spm and aiming for ground contact <320 ms.
recommendations.reason: Your May Z2 time is strong (45%), but cadence and ground contact variability (e.g., 316–286 ms) suggests inconsistent neuromuscular control — this session reinforces rhythm and efficiency within your dominant zone.

recommendations.action: Add one 8-minute threshold interval (Z3, HR 145–152 bpm) at 4:40–4:50 min/km pace during your longest run this week — preceded by 15 min warm-up and followed by 10 min cooldown.
recommendations.reason: Z3 time dropped from 26% last month to 16% this month, and your best recent pace (4:28 min/km on 2026-04-??) hasn’t been challenged since — this rebuilds lactate tolerance without overloading recovery.

recommendations.action: After your next run, perform 3 × 1-min strides (90% effort, ~3:50 min/km pace) with full 90-sec walk recovery, focusing on minimizing vertical oscillation (<7.5 cm) and landing midfoot.
recommendations.reason: Vertical oscillation rose from 7.1–7.7 cm in May’s middle runs to 8.1 cm on 2026-05-16 — strides reinforce efficient turnover and reduce bounce without requiring long distances.

weekly_focus.description: Reconnect neural control with mechanical efficiency: stabilize cadence and ground contact while reintroducing controlled intensity to preserve aerobic power and pace adaptability.
suggested_sessions: 4.5 km Zone 2 rhythm run (HR 128–138 bpm, cadence 145–147 spm)
6.5 km mixed-effort run (15 min Z2 → 8 min Z3 → 12 min Z2)
